script: Training a dog doesn't need harsh methods or special equipment. It needs clear signals, good timing and rewards your dog actually wants. Here are the five basics. One, name response. Say your dog's name in a happy voice, and reward them when they look at you. Two, sit. Hold a treat above the nose, move it back, and the moment their bottom touches the floor, say yes and reward. Three, come when called. Start indoors, back away, call once in an excited voice, and celebrate big when they arrive. Never call your dog to scold them, or they will learn that coming to you is unpleasant. Four, leave it. Close your fist around a treat, wait until they stop pushing, then reward them from your other hand. Five, loose leash walking. Stop moving whenever the leash goes tight, and move on when it softens. Keep sessions short, five minutes a few times a day, and end on a success. Dogs learn through repetition and consistency, so use the same words every time, and make sure everyone in your home does too. Patience matters more than perfection, and a well-timed treat will always beat a raised voice.
